During the process of parsing Kiro’s base URL, my region was set to ap-northeast-2, but there was no DNS entry for codewhisperer.ap-northeast-2.
When I fixed the region to us-east-2, it worked as expected.
Could you please take a look at this? And thank you very much for the great work.

```
@@ -192,7 +192,7 @@ export async function KiroAuthPlugin(_input: PluginInput): Promise<Hooks> {
         const token = await getKiroToken()
         if (!token) return {}

-        const region = token.region || "us-east-1"
+        const region = "us-east-1"
         const baseURL = `https://codewhisperer.${region}.amazonaws.com`

```

+ FYI

The issue appears to not always be a simple "provider is randomly dropping connections". In my case I could observe that the issue is rather a caused by broken PMTU (Path MTU Discovery) on my cellular data connection, rather than by the remote API itself.

In my particular case I was only observing these "connection resets" when I was connected through a mobile hotspot (Wi-Fi over 5G). The same CLI and the same API endpoint work reliably over a normal Wi-Fi connection.

In wireshark I could see some packets were silently dropped by the network path. A little test with ping utility let me confirm the results: ICMP packets above a certain size are dropped (`ping -D -s 1472` fails, while `ping -D -s 1360` succeeds). This indicates that packets are dropped and ICMP "packet too big" messages are not delivered back to the client.

As a workaround, lowering the MTU on the client network interface (en0 in my case) makes the connection work reliably also via cellular. However, this is a global workaround in Mac OS and as such not preferred, but might be the only one.

So if you want to fix this, try out `ping -D -s xxxx` which different values (going down from 1500) and then when it succeeds (1360 in my case), set your MTU to this value `sudo networksetup -setMTU en0 1360`. However, I assume you know what you are doing if you are messing with network setup on MacOS.

The preferred way in my opinion would be that the bun network stack is more conservative in general or could adapt to flaky networks through observed bahaviour. It's definitely not bun's fault if the network I am on breaks PMTU discovery, but a lot of applications (browsers etc.) do use heuristics and retry with smaller chunks etc. However, this is definitely not opencode's fault.

Just wanted to acknowledge this here, so whoever might have a similar setup may read this and lower their MTU to work around bun's network failing on such sketchy connections :)
